title: Sunrise & Sunset Protocols for Tokens and Components
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define explicit 'sunrise' (introduce) and 'sunset' (deprecate/remove) protocols for design tokens and UI components (buttons, tables, charts) so maintainers and contributors can reliably evolve the design system without surprising downstream consumers. This ticket collates the governance steps: contribution acceptance criteria, review checklist, RFC lifecycle, deprecation timelines, migration patterns, and observability signals. Goal is an actionable, low-friction process balancing forward progress with backward compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: A concise contribution checklist is available in the repo/confluence and referenced from PR templates
An RFC template exists for non-trivial token or component changes and an explicit review SLA is documented
Deprecation policy includes timelines (soft deprecation, warning, removal), communication channels, and migration helpers
A lightweight telemetry plan enumerates metrics to detect regressions and track migration adoption
Design + Frontend + Platform sign-off flows are documented and sample communications for breaking changes prepared
review_checklist: Design rationale: Why change is needed (short problem statement and alternatives considered)
Backward compatibility: API surface, token names, semantic meaning — list of breaking points
Migration path: codemods, theme mappings, and example before/after snippets
Accessibility: keyboard focus, contrast, semantics, and chart data labeling
Performance: bundle size impact and rendering cost for charts/tables
Testing: unit and visual regression tests included with PR
Docs: updated usage docs, deprecation notices, and cross-links to RFC when applicable
Stakeholders: ownership and affected teams enumerated (frontend, infra, SDKs)
Release impact: can change be rolled out incrementally (feature flag or opt-in)?
contribution_guidelines: Small cosmetic or token tweaks (<3 token changes) may be submitted directly with the design label and 48-hour review expectation
Component API changes or behavioral changes require an RFC (see RFC Process) before implementation
Always include migration guidance: mapping table of old->new tokens, codemod or example snippets
Add visual regression snapshots for UI components in the PR and reference the baseline commit
When introducing new tokens, prefer semantic tokens (e.g., color-bg-surface) rather than platform-specific names
For chart primitives, list backward-incompatible prop changes explicitly and provide a compatibility layer for one release cycle
Note any changes that may affect Dedicated/Private deployments and tag the infra/platform reviewers
rfc_process: When to write an RFC: API changes, token rename strategy, or any change likely to require migration assistance
RFC lifecycle: Draft -> Feedback (1 week, minimum) -> Design Review -> Engineering Feasibility Review -> Final decision
Decision owners: Design lead (final on semantics), Engineering lead (final on feasibility), Product for customer impact
Link RFC from PR description and include decision summary and accepted alternatives
Small RFCs may be fast-tracked with explicit approval from Design + Eng leads and documented as 'FastTrack' with rationale
deprecation_policy: Deprecation phases: Announcement (T0) -> Soft deprecation (warnings in console/docs, T+3 months) -> Removal (T+9 months)
Announcement must include migration path, sample codemod, and expected removal date
Soft deprecation: add deprecation banners to docs, emit runtime warnings where feasible (console.warn), and add linter rules to flag usage
Removal: remove implementation and docs, but keep a short 'removed in' entry in changelog for at least 12 months
Exceptions: security-critical removals or severe bugs may be expedited but require cross-org approval
Provide a compatibility package or shim for at least one release cycle for APIs widely used across internal products
rollout_and_migration: Canary rollout strategy: release new component behind a feature flag for apps with low latency requirements
Codemods: publish automated codemods in the repo with examples and a dry-run option
Migration playbooks: per-component playbook with steps to upgrade tokens, update stories, and run visual tests
Communication: publish deprecation posts in #design-system and weekly product engineering syncs; escalate to customers if high impact
Support window: offer 30-day office hours for high-impact migrations when removal date approaches
metrics_and_telemetry: Adoption: percentage of repos using new tokens vs old tokens (tracked by search + infra scans)
Usage: component render count in production (via instrumentation where available)
Regression signals: visual regression failures, increased bug reports tagged with design-system
Warning telemetry: runtime deprecation warnings count and top callers
Migration velocity: daily/weekly trend of codemod runs or PRs referencing the migration guide
decisions: Adopt semantic-first token naming convention for new tokens; plan for phased rename of popular legacy tokens
Require RFC for any public-facing component API change; small internal-only visual changes can bypass RFC with lead approval
Deprecation timeline standardized to 9 months for removal after announcement unless fast-tracked
Introduce a 'compatibility' npm package to host shims for one release cycle post-removal
